subject: RFP response: Dedicated capacity scenarios & GPU matrix for DeltaWorks
messages:
From: DeltaWorks Procurement <rfp@deltaworks.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwoodai.com, marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:05:12 -0700
Subject: RFP: Dedicated inference capacity — DeltaWorks

Hi Rafael / Marissa,

We're kicking off an RFP for dedicated inference capacity to support a multi-region deployment of our document understanding pipeline. Attached is our questionnaire; key asks:
- Preferred GPU families and supported memory/quantization options
- Expected throughput targets (tokens/sec and QPS) per model tier (baseline / peak)
- Reservation sizing: committed v. burst profiles and cushion for peak days
- Latency SLO targets (p50/p95/p99) and expected batch sizes
- Rollout/canary and fallback strategies when reserved capacity is saturated

Could you complete the attached questionnaire and include at least two capacity scenarios (cost-optimized and performance-optimized) with estimated monthly token costs? Our procurement deadline is 2027-05-24.

Thanks — Samir Shah (on behalf of DeltaWorks Procurement)

Attachment: DeltaWorks_RFP_Questions.pdf (application/pdf, 312KB)
From: rafael_mendes@redwoodai.com
To: marissa_cole@redwoodai.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com, priyom_das@redwoodai.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:12:45 -07:00
Subject: FW: RFP: Dedicated inference capacity — DeltaWorks (draft answers)

Team — forwarding DeltaWorks' questionnaire. I'm drafting a multi-scenario response (attached workbook). Primary asks for verification:
1) GPU mix: I'm leaning toward H100 80GB (performance) + A100 80GB (cost/perf) as the two representative families. Confirm whether we should also include an 8-bit quantized 4-bit fallback profile (q4_k) for cost scenario.
2) Throughput targets: I've put baseline/peak nominal numbers in tab 'throughput_assumptions' but need confirmation on per-model sequence lengths (they listed small/med/long).
3) Reservation cushions: proposing 20% cushion for first 6 months, with autoscaling burst to hosted pool for rare spikes. Is that acceptable commercially?

Attachments: capacity_scenarios_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet) — draft includes three scenarios: conservative, balanced, high-performance. Also gputype_profiles.md with kernel/quant notes.

I'll aim to send the completed questionnaire to Samir by EOD tomorrow, but want internal sign-off on numbers and the MAP (mutual action plan) timeline.

Rafael Mendes
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwoodai.com
From: marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwoodai.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:02:08 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: RFP: Dedicated inference capacity — DeltaWorks (draft answers)

Rafael — quick notes inline:
- GPU mix: include H100-80GB (fp16/amp + q4_k) and A100-80GB (fp16 + q8_0) as primary. For cost scenario also include a quantized LLM variant on T4 (for embeddings/low-latency small models).
- Throughput: baseline = 15k tokens/sec aggregate, peak = 120k tokens/sec (10x for flash events). For QPS use-case (short prompts) estimate p50 latency 18ms on H100, p95 55ms, p99 110ms at reserved throughput.
- Reservation cushion: 25% for first quarter, reduce to 15% after usage stabilizes.
- Canary/fallback: propose canary at 5% of traffic for 48 hours, automated fallback to A100 or hosted tier after 30s queueing or 95th percentile latency breach.

I updated capacity_scenarios_v3.xlsx with these numbers (see tabs 'throughput_assumptions' and 'reservation_policy').

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: rafael_mendes@redwoodai.com
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@deltaworks.com>, DeltaWorks Procurement <rfp@deltaworks.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodai.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com, priyom_das@redwoodai.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:20:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated inference capacity — DeltaWorks — capacity scenarios and MAP

Samir — thanks for the questionnaire. Please find our completed response attached along with a compact Capacity Scenario workbook and GPU profile notes. Highlights below and a short mutual action plan (MAP):

Highlights (executive summary):
- GPU families: H100-80GB (performance profile) and A100-80GB (balanced/cost profile). Optional T4 pool for low-memory/embeddings workloads in cost-optimized scenario. We include quantization profiles (q4_k / q8_0) with performance deltas in gputype_profiles.md.
- Throughput scenarios: conservative: 12k tokens/sec (reserved), balanced: 35k tokens/sec, performance: 120k tokens/sec peak with burst to hosted pool. See workbook for monthly unit cost estimates per scenario.
- SLOs: target p50/p95/p99 latencies of 12/45/100ms on H100 for short prompts (<=256 tokens). Long sequences expected to add linear per-token latency; workbook models these effects.
- Reservation sizing: recommend initial 3-month commit at the balanced profile with 25% cushion for month 1, taper to 15% months 2–3. Autoscaling burst policy into our hosted pool for infrequent >5x spikes.
- Rollouts: 48-hour 5% canary, automated rollback to A100 or hosted tier when queueing time exceeds 30s or p95 latency > baseline by 30%.

Mutual Action Plan (proposed):
1) Week 0: Sign NDA & finalize SOW (we can use your SOW template)
2) Week 1: Confirm model list and sequence length distributions (DeltaWorks)
3) Week 2–3: Provision reserved capacity (baseline) + run pre-production traffic tests with your tooling
4) Week 4: Canary (5% traffic) and SLA acceptance testing; handover to your infra team

Attachments: capacity_scenarios_v3.xlsx (detailed cost & throughput tabs), gputype_profiles.md (kernel/quant notes), completed RFP PDF.

If helpful, we can book a 30-minute technical walkthrough tomorrow; available 11:00–14:00 PT.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
rafel.mendes@redwoodai.com
Attachment stubs: capacity_scenarios_v3.xlsx (xlsx), gputype_profiles.md (text), DeltaWorks_RFP_Questions.pdf (pdf)

- We'd like to take the technical walkthrough Thursday 13:00 PT if that slot is still open.

I'll loop in our infra lead (cc'd privately) after internal review.

Regards,
Samir Shah
